method_resolution_asymmetry_note: Visomaster training samples are 224x224 (resized to model input), production substrates are at native ~219-373 px. lap_var measured at 224x224 is INFLATED relative to native lap_var. Train_visomaster lap_var (median ~120-380 across lanes) appears HIGHER than prod lap_var (median ~30-90), but a fair native-res comparison would likely show training is not nearly as sharp as the inflated numbers suggest. Direct cross-axis comparison should be treated as PROVISIONAL.

key_finding_train_eval_skin_frac_viso.interpretation: Train-vs-eval p50 ratio of 5.4x on visomaster_fake; even after accounting for resolution (training 224x224 vs eval ~360-380), this is a SIGNIFICANT train>eval asymmetry. But the direction is the OPPOSITE of what the user's cleanup hypothesis assumes: training viso fakes are SHARPER than eval viso fakes, not softer. So 'remove low-quality training samples to match production' would target a TINY tail of training, not a long tail.
